subject: Banking
title: App Outages and Access Risk
description: A fast breakdown of App Outages and Access Risk for builders.

hook.text: When Chime's app went down in 2019, millions of users couldn't access their money.

buildup.text: Digital-only banks have a single point of failure: the app.

discovery.text: Major bank outages increased 80% between 2019 and 2023.

twist.text: Some neobank customers keep a traditional bank account as backup. Digital convenience requires analog insurance.

climax.text: 100% digital means 100% dependent on technology. When the app breaks, the bank disappears.

punchline.text: App down equals bank closed. Digital-only banking has a single point of failure.

quiz.question: What happens when a neobank's app goes down?
options: Customers can't access their money at all

details.summary: As banking moves entirely to digital platforms, app outages leave customers unable to access their money. Major outages at banks like TSB, Chime, and Barclays have affected millions and raised questions about digital reliability.
details.whyItMatters: When your bank exists only on your phone, an outage means you cannot pay bills, buy groceries, or access funds. Digital banking concentrates risk in technology systems that can fail at the worst possible moments.
takeaways: TSB's 2018 migration failure locked 1.9 million customers out for weeks
Neobanks with no branches leave customers with zero alternatives during outages
Regulators are beginning to mandate operational resilience requirements

faq.question: What happens when a digital-only bank goes down?
faq.answer: Customers have no branch to visit and may be unable to access funds, make payments, or even prove their account exists. Extended outages have caused missed rent payments, bounced transactions, and significant financial stress.

faq.question: Are regulators addressing banking technology failures?
faq.answer: The UK and EU have introduced operational resilience frameworks requiring banks to identify critical services and maintain them during disruptions. Regulators now set maximum tolerable downtime standards for essential banking operations.
